def: A group that plays the adversary against a system, trying on purpose to make it fail so the failures can be fixed first.
The group that builds and defends the system being attacked.
A concrete, observable outcome an attacker is trying to cause, such as a refund above the limit or data sent to an outside address.
The share of attack attempts or goals that reached the goal under a stated attacker model and budget.
What the attacker may spend, such as queries, time, tools and knowledge of the system; an attack success rate means nothing without it.
The agreed limits of a red-team exercise: what is in scope, what is off limits and when to stop and report.
A recorded, reproducible way of reaching an attack goal, with enough detail for someone else to replay it and fix its cause.
An attack that uses the target's replies or scores as feedback to refine its next attempt.
Code or a model that decides whether an attack attempt reached its goal, preferably by checking observable effects.
After zero successes in n independent trials, the 95% upper bound on the success rate is about 3 divided by n.
An attack spread over several messages, each looking harmless alone, that escalates by building on the model's earlier replies.
